title: Theatre Royal
paragraphs: British literary-adaptation anthology produced by Harry Alan Towers for international syndication. The frozen 45-recording set carries OTRR sequence labels 1-48 with three gaps; secondary references disagree on total produced count, so sequence labels remain archive provenance rather than canonical production numbering.

GRH documents the program through Laurence Olivier-hosted first series (October 4, 1953 to April 18, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and Ralph Richardson-hosted second series (April 25, 1954 to September 1, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Harry Alan Towers (producer on 45 recordings and director on 5 recordings), Sidney Torch (music on 45 recordings and music director on 1 recording), Derek Patmore (radio adaptor on 30 recordings), Laurence Olivier (host on 26 recordings, performer on 12 recordings, and narrator on 1 recording), Ralph Richardson (host on 19 recordings, performer on 10 recordings, and narrator on 1 recording), Campbell Singer (performer on 4 recordings), and Charles Dickens (author on 3 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.244a08401c2c9142|WRVR-FM]] (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include classic literature and literary source, radio dramatization and adaptation, British stage and screen performance tradition, crime, guilt and moral transgression, supernatural, uncanny and gothic fiction, and social satire and class manners.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including British literary radio made for international transcription syndication, Prestige British stage and screen talent on radio, Classic literature adapted for postwar radio audiences, and Olivier-to-Richardson host succession.
